items.note: The page normalizes by V=Tp, tabulates the seven dominant powers with their margins, justifies the rows, shows that setup and repair are o(V), and adds, using the slack 2kappa as the paper does: "Half the smallest margin pays for logarithms and half remains as the saving." It also explains the striking feature correctly: g_2 is the product of three small factors, epsilon, c and 1-tau.

The substitution is written out for the binding cases ("g_2=2^{-75}2^{-56}2^{-50}=2^{-181}", "g_3=2^{-75}2^{-54}=2^{-129}"), and the rest are asserted by direct substitution, as in the paper. errors.quote: The permutations of [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md) are never executed, since they cancel
errors.problem: Only the retained source permutation R cancels in the convolution, by eq. (source-permutation-cancel): (RF_s^+)[(RF_s u)(RF_s v)]=(u*v)/S^2. The frequency permutation Q does not cancel. It is carried out by the chirp identity QF_t u = conj(a).(a*(conj(a).u))/T, so no separate permutation pass is needed, and its cost sits in the chirp and convolution rows.

errors.quote: an exchange acts on chunks of only $K=\Theta(p^{\epsilon c})$ bits and saves a factor $K^{-(1-\tau)}=p^{-\epsilon c(1-\tau)}$ against a full pass
errors.problem: One exchange costs O(VK^tau) by Lemma chunk-swap, which is more than a full pass of cost V. The saving factor K^{1-tau} is measured against the naive exchange by K full passes, O(VK), or equivalently against the whole layout done by plain scans (normalized p versus pK^{tau-1}). The phrase also writes the factor as 'saves a factor K^{-(1-tau)}' when it means the cost is multiplied by K^{-(1-tau)}.

errors.quote: With $\lg n=\max\{\lceil\log_2n\rceil,1\}$, within a constant factor of $\log n$ and at least $1$
errors.problem: At n=1, log n=0 while lg n=1, so lg n is within a constant factor of log n only for n>=2. That gap is why the paper uses lg n for the bound 'for every input length'.
